messages:
Ava: heads-up — we've been seeing a ton of tail latency coming from the gateway when requests fail early (auth/quota). allocation for the full request context + downstream sockets seems to be the expensive part.
Maya: can you share a sample p95 vs p99 breakdown?
Ava: p95 ~120ms, p99 ~950ms for requests that error out before hitting runtime. CPU/alloc spike correlates with goroutine churn.
Sam: my hunch: we're doing a full request pipeline (body buffers, filters, metrics) before we reject. if we can short-circuit on a cheap check we avoid most of that.
Liam: agree. two patterns: 1) pre-accept fast-path that can return 4xx/429 without allocating heavy resources; or 2) preflight LB that does auth introspect and only forwards valid requests. both have tradeoffs.
Zoe: pre-accept is attractive for Hosted mode — returns fast and saves us compute. but need to be careful about streaming clients expecting an open connection. short-circuit must be a proper HTTP response, not just drop.
Ava: proposal: introduce "accept-filter" stage at the TLS/HTTP mux level that runs a minimal rule-set: TLS SNI match, simple token signature check (no network introspect), allowlist, idempotency key dedupe using in-memory window. if pass => promote to full pipeline. if fail => immediate response + light metrics.
Maya: what about JWT introspection (opaque tokens)? that requires network calls to auth service. can't do that in fast path unless we cache.
Sam: we can maintain a small LRU cache for opaque-token -> allow/deny with ttl. cache miss falls back to full pipeline. need to be conservative about cache size.
Liam: also consider semantics for streaming endpoints: if client expects streaming, immediate 401 still fine, but if we short-circuit after we've started streaming headers it gets messy. so accept-filter must run pre-headers.
Ava: exactly — accept-filter must run before any headers are flushed. for HTTP/2/3 that means at the HEADERS frame. in practice we can intercept at request head parsing.
Zoe: metrics: add "gateway.origination_latency" (time from conn accept to short-circuit decision) and "gateway.promotion_ratio" (how many accepted into full pipeline). also tag by rule that triggered.
infra-bot: deploy-bot posted: new metric names registered: gateway.origination_latency, gateway.promotion_ratio, gateway.shortcircuit_reason_count.
Sam: implementation note: keep accept-filter single-threaded and lock-free paths for common checks (signed token verification using ed25519 public key), fall back to worker pool for expensive checks.
Maya: security tradeoff: cryptographic check in fast path is safe if keys rotate — need key caching and rotation hooks. and telemetry to surface false positives.
Liam: failure modes: 1) if accept-filter bugs, it can incorrectly reject valid traffic -> user-visible 401; 2) timing differences across regions if cache warms differently -> inconsistent behavior. mitigation: canary and header to force bypass.
Ava: on canary: add X-Edge-Accept-Bypass=true header for internal tests. also feature flag per cluster.
Zoe: what about idempotency dedupe? doing it in accept-filter reduces duplicate runtime work but we must ensure dedupe store is consistent for Dedicated/Private. maybe local window for Hosted, and an option to use central store.
Sam: agree. local dedupe is best-effort; for strict semantics customers can opt-in to central dedupe service.
Ava: quick config sketch:
```yaml
accept_filter:
  enabled: true
  rules:
    - name: signed_token
      type: signature_verify
      pubkeys: ["/etc/edge/keys/pubkey1.pem"]
    - name: ip_allowlist
      type: ip_check
    - name: idempotency_local_dedupe
      type: dedupe
      ttl_ms: 30000
```
Maya: nice. keep the config small to avoid long startup parsing.
Liam: tests: unit for rule logic, integration with harness simulating heavy erroring traffic, and a perf microbenchmark measuring allocations saved. aim for >3x reduction in allocations on short-circuit path.
Zoe: rollout plan: feature-flag behind canary; start with non-critical endpoints (health, health-check-related auth failures) then expand. collect promotion_ratio and error deltas.
Ava: action items: 1) I'll draft RFC with design + failure modes, 2) Sam to prototype accept-filter as a middleware in the edge mux, 3) Maya to add metrics and infra-bot to register alarms, 4) Zoe to own canary plan.
Sam: on it — I'll push a POC branch and post perf numbers here. :thumbsup:
Maya: will add metric dashboards and an alert for promotion_ratio < 0.6 during canary.
Liam: add note in RFC about header semantics for proxied clients (X-Redwood-Origination, X-Redwood-Shortcircuit-Reason).
Ava: thanks all — this should cut down wasted runtime cycles and make error paths predictable. :rocket:
